fact_check.claim: In a New York building with four or more residential units, landlord cannot unreasonably withhold consent to a sublease; consent must be advance and written
fact_check.note: RPL 226-b(2)(a): tenant in a building with four or more units may sublet with the landlord's advance written consent, which may not be unreasonably withheld.

fact_check.claim: Silence counts as consent (deemed consent)
fact_check.note: 226-b(2)(c): if the landlord sends nothing within the period, consent is deemed given.

fact_check.claim: Request must go by certified mail, return receipt requested
Request contents: term, subtenant name and addresses, reason, where tenant will live, co-tenant/guarantor written consent, copy of proposed sublease
fact_check.note: All six items match 226-b(2)(b).

fact_check.claim: Landlord has 10 days to ask for more information
fact_check.note: Law School page and statute (10 days of mailing, reasonable additional information) agree.

fact_check.claim: Landlord must respond within 30 days of the request or of the extra information, whichever is later
fact_check.note: Matches page and statute.

fact_check.claim: Subletting without consent is a 'substantial breach of lease or tenancy'
fact_check.note: 226-b(5): a sublet that does not follow the section is a substantial breach of lease or tenancy. The quoted phrase is accurate; the article's 'deposit and reference at risk' is the writer's inference.

fact_check.claim: Provisions waiving the section are void
Public housing and co-op proprietary leases are carved out by the statute
fact_check.note: 226-b(3): public housing/units with statutory admission criteria and cooperative shareholder proprietary leases excluded.

fact_check.claim: Building with three or fewer units: lease controls
fact_check.note: Page says right to sublease is controlled by the lease.

fact_check.claim: Government-subsidized apartments are excluded
fact_check.note: Page says protections do not apply to government-subsidized apartments.

fact_check.claim: Reasonable refusal: lease stays in force and you still owe remaining rent
fact_check.note: Matches, including the example of not following notice procedure.

fact_check.claim: Unreasonable refusal: you may sublet anyway; bad-faith landlord can owe legal costs
fact_check.note: 226-b(2)(c): tenant may sublet and recover court costs and attorney's fees if the owner acted in bad faith.

fact_check.claim: Original tenant remains liable under the lease after the subtenant moves in
fact_check.note: 226-b(2)(c): tenant remains liable under the lease. Law School page agrees.

fact_check.claim: Assignment: you are not liable if the new tenant fails to pay; unreasonable refusal obliges the landlord to end the lease on 30 days' notice
fact_check.note: Law School page says this. The statute (226-b(1)) frames it as the tenant requesting release on 30 days' notice, and says an owner may refuse an assignment without giving a reason. Article wording is acceptable but see fix about the assignment/sublet distinction.

fact_check.claim: Landlord may charge background/credit check fee, but no sublet fee not listed in the lease; any lease fee must be reasonable
fact_check.note: Fees section matches.

fact_check.claim: If subtenant stops paying, remedy is a claim in small claims court for example
fact_check.note: Page lists breach of contract claims in small claims, city, town/justice court or state supreme court.

fact_check.claim: Mutual termination is an option when the building bans subletting
fact_check.note: Page calls asking the landlord to end the lease early the most straightforward option. It does not tie this to buildings that ban subletting, but the use is reasonable.

fact_check.claim: Law School Tenants Advocacy Program hotline 607-301-1560
fact_check.note: Number appears on the page.

fact_check.claim: Cornell Off-Campus Living answers lease questions at 607-255-2310
fact_check.note: Number appears on the page, attributed to Off-Campus Living for lease and tenant-landlord questions.

fact_check.claim: Cornell lease checklist lists the ability to sublet and conditions for sublet
fact_check.note: Listed under Termination in 'Reviewing your lease'.

fact_check.claim: Marketplace has a Subleases section and a 'List/Find Sublets' option
fact_check.note: Both appear on the page.

fact_check.claim: Only people affiliated with Cornell, or who can prove it, can view and contact listers
fact_check.note: Page says only those affiliated or who can prove affiliation can view and contact.

fact_check.claim: Marketplace is free to use and particularly helpful for grad students who want to sublet
fact_check.note: Source says 'free to use for those with Cornell credentials' and especially useful for grad students. The article drops the Cornell-credentials condition, which is minor but a sublet lister should be told.

fact_check.claim: Off-Campus Living email list is a forum for people who want to sublet, open to the Cornell community with a NetID
fact_check.note: Page confirms forum for offering a sublet, Cornell community, NetID needed (acceptance letter route exists without NetID).

fact_check.claim: Cornell lists the Daily Sun, Ithacarents.com, the Ithaca Journal and the Ithaca Times but does not endorse them
fact_check.note: List and non-endorsement are correct. But the page says Ithacarents.com only allows members of the Landlords Association of Tompkins County to post, so it is not a place a tenant can list a sublet. The article presents it under 'Where to list' without that.

fact_check.claim: Cornell advice: view properties in person and read the whole lease before signing or paying
fact_check.note: Quote on the page matches.

fact_check.claim: Public listings on Craigslist and similar sites work, and they also reach scammers
fact_check.note: No source link. Reads as fact, not marked as the writer's advice. Reword as advice or drop.

fact_check.claim: Some landlords require subtenants to be students or pass the same screening as any tenant
fact_check.note: No source link. The searched web has a Cornell-area landlord page requiring a Cornell student subtenant, but the article cites nothing. Either link an example landlord page or label it as 'some landlords may'. Also no sublet fee example is given.

beats_top.query: cornell summer sublet how to sublet apartment ithaca landlord permission
beats_top.why: The #1 result I could identify is Cornell's short subletting page, which gives only the general idea, the marketplace database and the Off-Campus Living phone number. I could not open it myself (404 when fetched), so this judgment rests on the search summary. Ours answers the permission question in the first paragraph with the statute, the 10-day and 30-day clock, deemed consent, fees and where to list.
changes: State plainly near the top that a subletter in a 3-or-fewer-unit building or subsidized unit has no statutory right, which the page does, but add a one-line 'what to do first' decision (count units, check lease).
Remove or qualify Ithacarents.com as a place for a tenant to list.
Add a concrete landlord example with sublet fee and subtenant rules, linked to an official landlord page, so 'usual fees' is answered; currently the answer is only 'check your lease'.

fixes: In the 'Other sites' bullet under Where to list, say that Ithacarents.com only lets members of the Landlords Association of Tompkins County post, so a tenant cannot list a sublet there; source https://scl.cornell.edu/residential-life/housing/campus-housing/housing-search-process/rental-listings-resources. Keep the Daily Sun, Ithaca Journal and Ithaca Times as the options Cornell lists and keep the non-endorsement.

Reword 'Public listings on Craigslist and similar sites work, and they also reach scammers' as the writer's own advice (for example 'Our view: public sites reach more people and also more scammers') or delete it; it has no source.

In step 2, change 'Some landlords require subtenants to be students or to pass the same screening as any tenant' to 'Some landlords may require...' and either link one Ithaca landlord's official tenant page that states such a rule, or add that it is an example of what to ask about, not a finding.

In the Cornell Graduate School sentence under Cornell's Off-Campus Housing Marketplace, change 'free to use' to 'free to use for those with Cornell credentials'; source https://www.gradschool.cornell.edu/announcements/grad-tips-renting/.

In 'Leaving for good', add that under the statute (https://www.nysenate.gov/legislation/laws/RPP/226-B) an owner may refuse an assignment without giving a reason, and that the remedy for an unreasonable refusal is the tenant's right to request release on 30 days' notice, so the reader does not assume an assignment is easier to get than a sublet.

In the Fees section, add one sentence that says plainly that the usual Ithaca sublet fee could not be sourced, and point to the landlord's own policy as the place to ask; keep the existing statement, and do not add any dollar figure unless it comes from an official landlord page you link.
